cards.name: Run acceleration and momentum
cards.summary: Holding run adds a ramping bonus to horizontal speed, with a higher ceiling while the speed booster item is equipped.
cards.behavior: While the character is in the running movement type and the run button is held, a separate bonus speed grows by one sixteenth of a pixel per frame (0x1000 of 65536 subpixel units). Without the speed booster item the bonus stops at 2 pixels per frame. With the speed booster item equipped it stops at 7 pixels per frame, and the first frame of this state also sets the momentum flag and starts the booster charge counter. Releasing run or leaving the running type adds nothing more. Standing in water, lava or acid (when the gravity suit is not equipped) also adds nothing, and the bonus is reset to zero unless the momentum flag is set. Entering lava cancels an active speed boost. In a jump the whole part of the bonus is halved and added to the jump impulse, and the fractional part is added unchanged, only when the speed booster item is equipped.

constants.name: runBonusStep
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame added each frame at 60 Hz (0.0625 pixels/frame per frame)

constants.name: runBonusCap
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz, speed booster not equipped

constants.name: boostedRunBonusCap
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz, speed booster equipped

cards.name: Jump impulse and press duration
cards.summary: A jump replaces vertical velocity with a fixed upward impulse whose size depends on hi-jump boots, liquid state and the speed booster.
cards.behavior: The impulse is a whole-pixel word plus a 16-bit fractional word, in pixels per frame. A normal jump starts at 4.875 pixels per frame (4 + 0xE000/65536). Hi-jump boots raise it to 6.0. In water the impulse drops to 1.75, or 2.5 with hi-jump boots. In lava or acid it is 2.75, or 3.5 with hi-jump boots. The gravity suit ignores liquid and uses the dry values. Holding the jump button keeps the upward thrust going; releasing it, or reaching zero upward speed, zeroes the speed and switches to falling, so press duration sets jump height. With the speed booster item equipped, half of the whole-pixel run bonus and all of its fraction are added to the impulse.

constants.name: baseJumpSpeed
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz (vertical impulse whole word); decoded impulse with fraction is 4.875 pixels/frame

constants.name: baseJumpFraction
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame at 60 Hz (0.875 pixels/frame)

constants.name: highJumpSpeed
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz (whole word; fraction 0, decoded 6.0), hi-jump boots equipped, dry

constants.name: waterJumpSpeed
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz (whole word); decoded impulse with fraction is 1.75 pixels/frame, no hi-jump, no gravity suit

constants.name: waterJumpFraction
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame at 60 Hz (0.75 pixels/frame); lava and acid use the same fraction with whole word 2, decoded 2.75

constants.name: highJumpWaterSpeed
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz (whole word) with fraction 0x8000, decoded 2.5 in water with hi-jump boots; lava and acid use whole word 3, decoded 3.5

cards.name: Wall jump
cards.summary: A wall contact while spinning in the air lets the player kick off with a new upward impulse.
cards.behavior: A wall jump is checked only when the last distinct movement type was a spin jump or a previous wall jump. The spin animation must first reach frame 11 (frame 27 for the screw attack pose); before that, touching a wall only rewinds the animation. After that, the wall jump fires when the player holds a horizontal direction toward a wall that the collision check reports, and presses jump anew. The vertical impulse replaces the vertical speed with 4.625 pixels per frame dry, or 5.5 with hi-jump boots. In water it is 0.25, or 0.5 with hi-jump boots. In lava or acid it is 2.625, or 3.5 with hi-jump boots. The gravity suit ignores liquid. With the speed booster item equipped, the run bonus is added as for a normal jump. The action resets the grapple wall-jump timer. The impulse is set only on the frame the movement type changes into wall jumping.

constants.name: wallJumpSpeed
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz (vertical impulse whole word); decoded impulse with fraction is 4.625 pixels/frame, dry, no hi-jump

constants.name: wallJumpFraction
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame at 60 Hz (0.625 pixels/frame); lava and acid use the same fraction with whole word 2, decoded 2.625

constants.name: highJumpWallSpeed
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz (whole word); decoded impulse with fraction is 5.5 pixels/frame, dry, hi-jump boots

constants.name: highJumpWallFraction
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame at 60 Hz (0.5 pixels/frame), same for dry, water, lava and acid with hi-jump boots

constants.name: waterWallJumpFraction
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame at 60 Hz (0.25 pixels/frame); whole word is 0, so water wall jump impulse is 0.25 pixels/frame without hi-jump boots

cards.name: Gravity and fall speed
cards.summary: Airborne motion uses subpixel gravity with separate strengths for air, water, and lava or acid.
cards.behavior: Each airborne frame adds a gravity step to the vertical speed while falling, and the add stops once the whole-pixel part of the fall speed equals 5 (so the speed settles just above 5 pixels per frame, not clamped exactly). Dry gravity is 0x1C00/65536, about 0.109 pixels per frame each frame. Water uses 0x800, 0.031. Lava and acid use 0x900, about 0.035. The gravity suit selects the dry value everywhere. Rising motion subtracts the same step each frame, with no cap. Leaving a liquid restores dry gravity.

constants.name: airGravity
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame added each frame at 60 Hz (0.109375 pixels/frame per frame)

constants.name: waterGravity
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame added each frame at 60 Hz (0.03125 pixels/frame per frame)

constants.name: lavaGravity
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame added each frame at 60 Hz (0.03516 pixels/frame per frame), lava and acid

constants.name: terminalFallSpeed
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz (whole-word value at which gravity stops being added; the speed can end slightly above 5.0)

cards.name: Water and lava movement
cards.summary: Liquid states swap the jump impulse, gravity, and horizontal speed table for submerged movement.
cards.behavior: Water and lava or acid are chosen from the liquid heights relative to the bottom of the character. Entering water selects the dedicated water horizontal speed table, a lighter gravity and a smaller jump impulse. Lava and acid select their own horizontal table, gravity and jump values. Without the gravity suit, lava adds 0.5 health per frame of periodic damage and acid adds 1.5 health per frame; the periodic damage is then halved by the varia suit and quartered by the gravity suit. The gravity suit also stops lava damage and ignores all liquid overrides for jumps, gravity and horizontal speed. Entering lava cancels an active speed boost. Ambient water detection also drives splash and bubble effects.

constants.name: waterJumpSpeed
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz (vertical impulse high word)

constants.name: waterJumpFraction
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: waterGravity
constants.unit: 1/65536 pixel per frame each frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: lavaDamagePerFrame
constants.unit: 1/65536 health per frame at 60 Hz (0.5 health/frame), no gravity suit, before suit division

constants.name: acidDamagePerFrame
constants.unit: health per frame at 60 Hz whole word, plus 0x8000 subunits, decoded 1.5 health/frame, before suit division

cards.name: Morph-ball bombs
cards.summary: Bombs dropped in ball form use a one-second fuse and a shared limit on active bombs.
cards.behavior: A new press of fire in ball form with the bombs item places a bomb in one of five projectile slots. The fuse counter starts at 60 frames, the animation advances at 15 frames left, and the bomb explodes at zero. At most 5 bombs may be live. Once at least one bomb is live, each further placement also needs the cooldown to reach zero after the previous placement, and the cooldown is set to 16 frames per placement. Power bombs use the same slots and a 60-frame fuse, spend one ammunition, set a 40-frame cooldown, and only one power bomb may be live at a time.

constants.name: bombFuse
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (one second)

constants.name: bombPlacementCooldown
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (16 frames, about 0.27 seconds), applies only while another bomb is live

constants.name: maxActiveBombs
constants.unit: bombs (count of live bombs; checked once per frame at 60 Hz)

constants.name: powerBombCooldown
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (40 frames, about 0.67 seconds)

cards.name: Beam fire cadence
cards.summary: Uncharged beam shots use a short cooldown when tapped and a longer one when the fire button is held.
cards.behavior: A new press of fire spawns one uncharged shot and sets a 15-frame cooldown (12 for one beam combination). Without the charge beam, holding fire repeats shots on a 25-frame cadence instead. With the charge beam equipped the 15-frame value is used for every shot. At most 5 beam shots may be live at once. Firing starts a ten-frame window in which the check for the player being hit by his own projectiles is skipped. A charged shot uses a 30-frame cooldown. Beam type selects the projectile handler and sound.

constants.name: tapCooldown
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (15 frames, 0.25 seconds; table value for most beam combinations)

constants.name: holdCooldown
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (25 frames, about 0.42 seconds), auto-fire hold without the charge beam

constants.name: selfHitGrace
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz

cards.name: Charged beam timing
cards.summary: Holding fire charges a beam; releasing after one second fires a charged shot, and two seconds triggers a special attack.
cards.behavior: Charging needs the charge beam and no hyper beam. The charge counter advances each frame while fire is held, and the first frame of a hold also fires an uncharged shot at once. Releasing before 60 frames fires another uncharged shot. Releasing at 60 frames or later fires a charged beam. Holding to 120 frames spends the charge on the special beam attack when one is available; the counter stops growing at 120. Charging also changes the suit palette and the flare animation.

constants.name: chargeThreshold
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (one second)

constants.name: specialChargeThreshold
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (two seconds)

constants.name: chargedBeamCooldown
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (0.5 seconds) before the next beam shot

cards.name: Shinespark
cards.summary: Activating a stored speed charge starts a windup, then a fast rocket flight that drains energy and ends on a wall hit or at low energy.
cards.behavior: Starting the spark clears vertical and base speed, sets the boost counter to 1024 and the horizontal run speed to 8 pixels per frame, and begins a 30-frame windup. The shine timer starts at 60 frames and is refreshed to 15 frames on each flight frame. During flight the horizontal run speed grows each frame by the vertical acceleration step and is capped at 15 pixels per frame. The vertical displacement is clamped to 14 pixels per frame. The contact damage index is set to the spark value so enemies are hurt on touch. Energy drops by 1 each frame while health is at least 30. The flight ends on a wall hit or when health is below 30, and then a crash sequence plays.

constants.name: sparkWindup
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (half a second)

constants.name: sparkShineTimerStart
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (one second)

constants.name: sparkShineTimerRefresh
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz, set on each flight frame

constants.name: sparkStartSpeed
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz (horizontal run speed at the start)

constants.name: sparkHorizontalSpeedCap
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: sparkVerticalSpeedCap
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: sparkEnergyFloor
constants.unit: health points; the spark ends below this value

constants.name: boostedRunBonusCap
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz, run bonus ceiling with the speed booster

cards.name: Enemy contact damage
cards.summary: Contact with a damaging enemy applies suit-filtered damage, a long invulnerability window, and a short knockback.
cards.behavior: When a damaging enemy touches the player, no contact-damage state is active and the player is not invincible, the enemy damage passes through suit division. The gravity suit quarters it, and otherwise the varia suit halves it; the two do not stack. The hit grants 96 frames of invincibility and 5 frames of knockback away from the enemy. A separate contact-damage state (speed boost, shinespark, screw attack) lets the player damage enemies by touch instead.

constants.name: touchInvincibility
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (1.6 seconds)

constants.name: touchKnockback
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz

constants.name: gravitySuitDamageShift
constants.unit: bit shift applied once per hit (divide damage by four), gravity suit takes priority over varia

constants.name: variaSuitDamageShift
constants.unit: bit shift applied once per hit (divide damage by two), varia suit without gravity suit

cards.name: Spike and hazard blocks
cards.summary: Spike and hazard blocks apply fixed damage with a one-second invulnerability window and a longer knockback.
cards.behavior: A standard spike block adds 16 raw damage, grants 60 frames of invincibility and 10 frames of knockback. One spike variant adds 60 raw damage instead; in the area numbered 3 it hurts only once that area's boss flag is set. The airborne spike variant also needs no active contact-damage state. Damage applies only when no invincibility timer is active, and the knockback direction comes from the facing. The raw damage then passes through periodic-damage handling, where the varia suit halves it and the gravity suit quarters it.

constants.name: spikeDamage
constants.unit: health points per contact, evaluated each frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: spikeInvincibility
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (one second)

constants.name: spikeKnockback
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz

constants.name: heavySpikeDamage
constants.unit: health points per contact, evaluated each frame at 60 Hz

cards.name: Camera anchoring and follow
cards.summary: The camera follows the player's movement with a side-dependent screen anchor and catches up at the player's speed plus one pixel per frame.
cards.behavior: While the player stays off the ideal camera position, the camera origin moves by the player's measured displacement plus one extra pixel each frame, while it moves toward a side-dependent anchor. Facing right places the player 96 pixels from the left screen edge, and facing left places the player 160 pixels from the left edge (default camera distance index; other indices use 80/64, 32/32 and 224/224 pixels). Knockback and some movement types swap the sides. Vertical scrolling uses separate up and down anchors taken from the room header. While the grapple beam sets the slow scrolling flag, the camera moves 3 pixels per frame toward a dead zone around the player (horizontal 96 to 160, vertical 112 to 144 pixels from the screen origin).

constants.name: faceRightAnchor
constants.unit: pixels from the screen left edge on a 256-pixel-wide screen

constants.name: faceLeftAnchor
constants.unit: pixels from the screen left edge on a 256-pixel-wide screen

constants.name: slowScrollStep
constants.unit: pixels/frame at 60 Hz, grapple-beam slow scrolling

cards.name: Door and elevator transition
cards.summary: Room changes run as a timed sequence that freezes play, fades, loads the next room, aligns the camera, and returns control.
cards.behavior: The transition coroutine keeps the world drawing while it waits for sound to drain, fades the palette, loads the door header and room data, then scrolls the layer origin one pixel per frame until its low byte is zero. A downward elevator waits 48 frames before the load; an upward elevator skips the wait. The player is placed at the destination door and the screen fades back in. Sound and music queues are cleared during the load.

constants.name: elevatorHold
constants.unit: frames at 60 Hz (0.8 seconds), downward elevators only

cards.name: Sixty-hertz frame pacing
cards.summary: The host runs one emulated frame per loop and falls back to a repeating millisecond delay to hold sixty frames per second.
cards.behavior: Each loop iteration collects input and runs exactly one emulated frame. When vertical sync is not pacing the loop and rendering is on, the host adds 17, 17 or 16 milliseconds to a target tick by frame number modulo 3 and sleeps until it. The pattern averages 16.67 milliseconds, 60 frames per second. If the loop falls more than 500 milliseconds behind, the target clock resets. Turbo mode skips rendering on most frames while still running the simulation.

constants.name: firstFrameDelay
constants.unit: milliseconds per frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: secondFrameDelay
constants.unit: milliseconds per frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: thirdFrameDelay
constants.unit: milliseconds per frame at 60 Hz

cards.name: Reserve energy transfer
cards.summary: Pressing the action button in the tank menu starts a reserve transfer that adds one health point per frame to main health.
cards.behavior: In the equipment screen tank category, a new press of the A button starts a transfer. The delay counter is seeded from the reserve amount rounded up to a multiple of 8. Each frame the counter drops by one, main health gains 1, and reserve loses 1; a sound plays every 8 frames. The transfer continues without further button input. It ends when reserve reaches zero or main health reaches its maximum, where the code clamps health and clears the reserve value.

constants.name: reserveTransferRate
constants.unit: health points/frame at 60 Hz, applied to both main gain and reserve loss
